hero.title: Why Kind Health Tech exists
hero.subtitle: The public record of our purpose statement — the impact we intend on society and the environment, how it is inseparable from our business model, and the board resolution that adopted it.

statement.quote: Kind Health Tech exists to return the value of handmade textiles to the hands that make them. We build and operate the commerce and production platform through which verified artisans around the world sell their handcrafted work directly to buyers — the maker's name on every piece, a fair and transparent share of every sale, and the heavy work of verification, quality control, logistics, payments and compliance carried by us, not by them. Through this we intend two specific impacts: craft livelihoods that endure because they are profitable, and garments that are traced, honest and low-waste — made in small batches from verified materials, with every claim auditable.
statement.attribution: Adopted by resolution of the Board of Directors of Kind Health Tech SIA

impact.eyebrow: What the purpose commits us to
impact.title: Two impacts, kept specific.
impact.lead: The purpose is not aspiration — it names who benefits and how. These are the commitments the company holds itself to, and the practices already running on the platform.

items.title: Direct trade, fair share
items.body: Artisans sell on storefronts we operate with them. Payout terms are published, settlements arrive in the artisan's own currency, and the layers of middlemen who historically captured their margin are designed out of the rails.

items.title: The maker's name on every piece
items.body: Every garment is linked to the individual who made it — name, role and years on the loom travel with the product. Craft becomes credited, visible work rather than anonymous factory output.

items.title: Work routed to where craft lives
items.body: Production is dispatched to vetted ateliers and handloom clusters — Bagru, Srinagar, Florence — with mobile-first tools, so artisans join global commerce without leaving their village or learning a portal. 150+ artisans onboarded to date.

items.title: Heritage that pays for itself
items.body: Handloom weaving, hand-block printing and natural dyeing survive only if they earn. We route demand to these techniques so the next generation inherits working craft, not museum pieces.

items.title: Made to order, not to landfill
items.body: Runs are produced in small batches matched to real demand, cutting the overproduction that makes fashion one of the world's most wasteful industries.

items.title: Provenance as fact
items.body: Materials are traced to the lot, the loom and the village; certifications such as GOTS are verified on the platform; and every piece ships with a Digital Product Passport aligned to the EU ESPR — environmental claims become auditable facts, not storytelling.

items.title: Natural materials first
items.body: We prioritise natural fibres and dyes — cashmere, silk, natural indigo — and log every dye, weave and finish step with timestamps.

items.title: Waste designed out
items.body: Digitised inventory and step-level production tracking mean materials are ordered against real need, with reorder alerts firing before waste happens — not after.

strategy.title: The purpose is the product, not a programme.
strategy.lead: Every line of revenue runs through the purpose: the company earns only when verified artisans sell directly. The impact and the business case are the same motion.

pillars.practice: Every artisan is vetted before they can sell on the platform, and we carry quality control, logistics, payments and compliance on their behalf.
pillars.relevance: Buyers pay because unverified sellers cannot join — the core service the company monetises is the same service that protects makers and customers.

pillars.practice: Maker IDs, lot-level material tracing and Digital Product Passports (EU ESPR) are built into the platform core — not bolted on as marketing.
pillars.relevance: Transparency is a feature customers pay for and regulators increasingly require; it turns the artisan's story into a commercial advantage.

pillars.practice: We run commerce end to end — storefronts on custom domains, marketplace and social channels, payments, fulfilment — with the maker credited on every product page.
pillars.relevance: Revenue grows only when artisans sell directly, so the company's growth metric and its social impact are the same number.

pillars.practice: Published commission, transparent payout terms and settlement in the artisan's currency are platform features, not charity programmes.
pillars.relevance: Artisans stay because the economics are honest — retention is the business case for fairness.
